artifacts.summary: Verifies task 122's precondition is met; evaluates the --lit/Stage 3.6 acceptance criterion (lit_flag reaches every teammate, but literature resolution runs once per teammate rather than once-and-shared -- a deliberate task-122 design choice, not a defect, since orchestrator_mode structurally forecloses the named interactive-firing risk); and maps the real deletion blast radius (18 source-store files beyond the 3 skill directories, including a test fixture and a stale synthesis-agent.md docstring).

memory_candidates.content: In skill-orchestrate's Stage 3.6 Team Fan-Out, Stage 3.5 Dispatch Prep (memory retrieval + --lit literature-briefing resolution) is deliberately called once PER TEAMMATE inside the spawn loop, not once and shared -- this is documented design intent (task 122 research report Decision 5), not an oversight. It is safe under orchestrator_mode=true because the shared lit-stage4a-flow.md's interactive AskUserQuestion branches are structurally unreachable whenever orchestrator_mode is true (the deterministic [lit:auto] autonomous fallback always applies instead), so repeated per-teammate resolution cannot trigger repeated interactive prompts -- it is merely redundant subprocess/search work, not a correctness bug.

When a task's WORK section says 'delete skill X, grep for zero hits', do a repo-wide grep for the skill's own name across the source store BEFORE scoping the plan -- deletion tasks in this repo routinely under-scope their own blast radius (commands' routing dispatch code, agent docstrings referencing the skill by name, manifest.json's flat provides.skills array, context/patterns prose, and test fixtures that read the file path directly all count as hits and must be resolved for the zero-hits acceptance criterion to actually pass).
